{
  "verdict": "PARTIAL",
  "confidence_0_to_1": 0.72,
  "key_evidence_supporting": [
    "Implements a DP over Pauli paths consistent with the paper’s uniform-noise/Pauli-path truncation description and uses local factorization to avoid 4^n blowup",
    "Shows exact agreement with full density-matrix (Kraus) simulation at machine precision once ℓ is large enough to include all contributing paths (sanity/correctness check)",
    "Empirically observes RMS truncation error decreasing with increasing noise strength γ at fixed ℓ, matching the paper’s core intuition that noise damps high-weight contributions",
    "Tracks number of retained low-weight paths and observes weak dependence on n for fixed ℓ in tested brick-wall circuits, consistent with polynomial-in-n behavior for fixed truncation"
  ],
  "key_evidence_against": [
    "Does not test the paper’s stated success criterion over “most input states drawn from an ensemble” (they appear to use a fixed observable and do not report an input-state ensemble/RMS over inputs as in Theorem 1)",
    "Complexity evidence is limited to small n (≤10), fixed depth (d=3), and a specific 1D brick-wall architecture; does not substantiate the theorem’s general-circuit scaling claims",
    "Theorem-1-style parameter scaling (runtime/error vs ε, γ) is not validated beyond qualitative monotonicity; no check of the stated quasipolynomial/exponential-in-1/γ dependence",
    "Algorithm 2 (gate-based noise) and the sampling/anticoncentration extension are explicitly untested"
  ],
  "scope_covered": [
    "Core Algorithm 1 mechanics for uniform local depolarizing noise (Pauli-path DP with truncation)",
    "Correctness in the limit of no truncation (ℓ large) by comparison to exact Kraus simulation on small instances",
    "Qualitative truncation-error behavior vs noise strength γ on a random-circuit ensemble (over circuits, not inputs)",
    "Empirical retained-path-count behavior vs n for fixed ℓ on a specific circuit family"
  ],
  "scope_not_covered": [
    "Full Theorem 1 guarantee as stated (success on most input states from allowed ensembles; RMS over inputs; stated ε- and γ-dependent complexity bound)",
    "Theorem 2 / Algorithm 2 for gate-based noise (quasipolynomial-time analogue)",
    "Sampling-from-output-distribution corollary under anticoncentration",
    "Error-mitigation implication corollaries beyond informal acceptance"
  ],
  "one_line_summary": "The replication credibly implements and sanity-checks the uniform-noise Pauli-path truncation algorithm on small circuits, but does not fully reproduce Theorem 1’s stated ensemble-over-inputs and complexity-scaling guarantees, leaving major parts of the paper untested."
}
